alt: Infographic: the GMAT Focus exam at a glance (three sections: Quant, Verbal, Data Insights; total score 205-805).

Infographic titled How Your GMAT Score Works. Cards Quant 60–90, Verbal 60–90 and Data Insights 60–90 are added together into a Total 205–805 card. Caption: All three sections count equally. Scale markers: 555 ≈ 47th percentile, 655 ≈ 90th percentile, 705 ≈ 98th percentile. Footnote: Percentiles are approximate.

Infographic titled Your 10-Month GMAT Journey: a winding road with seven milestones in order: Oct 2026 · Orientation, Nov · Foundations, Dec–Feb · Core Skills, Mar–Jun · Advanced Practice, Jul–Aug · Mock Season, 28 Aug 2027 · Test Day, Sep 2027 onward · Applications.
Infographic titled The Learning Loop: a cycle of five steps, Learn the idea, Practise it, Review your mistakes, Space it out, Test yourself, with the word Repeat in the centre.

Infographic titled Why Did I Get It Wrong? Five reasons and fixes: Concept gap, Re-read the lesson; Careless slip, Slow down on the last step; Misread the question, Reread before answering; Ran out of time, Practise timed sets; Fell for a trap, Name the trap in your log.

Infographic titled Anatomy of a GMAT Argument: two Premise boxes feed an arrow into a Conclusion box; a dashed bridge on the arrow is labelled Assumption (the hidden gap). Caption: Find the gap. Most questions are about it.

Infographic titled Critical Reasoning Question Types, nine cards: Assumption, Find the missing link; Strengthen, Close the gap; Weaken, Open the gap; Evaluate, Ask the key question; Inference, Stay inside the facts; Paradox, Make both facts true; Boldface, Name each part's role; Flaw, Spot the bad logic; Complete, Fill the blank logically.

Infographic titled Map the Passage, Not the Details: a three-paragraph document beside a notepad reading P1: Context, P2: Author's view, P3: Counterpoint, Tone: Cautiously optimistic. Caption: One line per paragraph. Details can wait.

Infographic titled Five Data Insights Question Types: Data Sufficiency, Is there enough info?; Table Analysis, Sort and test 3 statements; Graphics Interpretation, Read the graph, fill 2 blanks; Two-Part Analysis, Two linked answers; Multi-Source Reasoning, Combine 2–3 tabs.

Infographic titled Percent Change Made Simple. Formula: Percent change = (New − Old) ÷ Old × 100. Multiplier chips: Up 20% → × 1.2 and Down 20% → × 0.8. Example: Up 20%, then down 20%: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, a 4% drop overall.

Infographic titled Distance = Rate × Time: a triangle with Distance on top and Rate and Time on the bottom. Caption: Cover what you want, the rest shows the formula. Note: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
Infographic titled Overlapping Sets: two overlapping circles A and B, the overlap labelled Both, the outside area labelled Neither. Formula: Total = A + B − Both + Neither.

Infographic titled Pacing Checkpoints. Quant: Question 7 by 15 min, Question 14 by 30 min, Question 21 by 45 min. Verbal: Question 8 by 15 min, Question 16 by 30 min, Question 23 by 45 min. Data Insights: Question 7 by 15 min, Question 14 by 30 min, Question 20 by 45 min. Caption: Behind by 3+ minutes? Make a smart guess and move on.

Infographic titled Test Day Checklist: Passport (name matches your booking); Arrive 30 minutes early; Light breakfast and water; Snack for the break; Your practised section order; Breathe. You are ready.

Infographic titled Your Three Paths After the GMAT: ISB PGP, India, 2028 intake; Masters in Management or Marketing, Europe, 2028 intake; Experienced MBA, India or abroad, Later, with 4+ years. Caption: Your GMAT score stays valid for 5 years.

Infographic titled Why Spaced Review Works: a steeply falling curve labelled Without review, and a stepped curve that stays high labelled With spaced review, with review points marked Day 1, Day 3, Day 7 and Day 16.
